$comment: Which payload mapper applies to which return period, and which official schema files validate it. To support a new portal format: drop the new schema files in this folder, add a version entry here (set the previous entry's effectiveTo), add one mapper file named after the id, and register it in src/domain/gst/returns/mappers/index.ts. No migration, no change to the calculations. effectiveFrom/effectiveTo are return periods as YYYY-MM (inclusive); null means unbounded. Nothing below states a date the portal has not published: unknown stays null.

versions.notes: Official Save request schema. Payment of tax (tx_pmt) and liab_breakup are not produced: they come from GSTN ledgers.

Official Save request schema (additionalProperties is false throughout, so only schema-named keys are written). Written: b2b, b2cl, b2cs, cdnr, cdnur, exp, nil, hsn (b2b/b2c) and doc_issue. Not computed yet: advances, e-commerce and amendments. The Submit schema (gstin, ret_period) is the filing call and is not used: filing needs a GSP and a signature.

Official Save request schema, validated. Which key is which row is read from the form and the GSTR-9 Offline Tool v2.2, not confirmed by a sample file, so every export is a draft. Rows the engine does not compute are omitted (never zero) so the portal keeps what was entered. Table 8 is not written: the schema's descriptions of its keys are copied from other rows. 6A, 6A1, 6A2, 6J and 6O are computed by the portal; 6A1, 6A2 and 8H1 exist in the Offline Tool but not in this schema.

Inbound: the portal's Get Cash Ledger Details response. The schema is inconsistent with itself: it requires refNo but names the property ref_no, and requires igstbal, cgstbal, sgstbal and cessbal inside op_bal and cl_bal, which define igst, cgst, sgst and cess instead. Those four balance keys and refNo are dropped from required (they are not used). Free-text patterns (desc) are reported as warnings, not refusals.
